annotation.title_clean: Labour rights for journalists and media professionals as a safeguard for independence and truthful information
annotation.title_en: Labour rights for journalists and media professionals as a safeguard for independence and truthful information
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C series
annotation.summary_en: European Economic and Social Committee opinion on journalists' labour rights, covering precarious work, bogus self-employment, burnout, harassment and media funding. It briefly addresses generative AI in newsrooms, calling for monitoring of EU AI rules, social dialogue on AI and AI literacy funding. No embodied AI content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Calls for full application of the European Media Freedom Act and support for media outlets, including a possible VAT reduction.
Urges social dialogue, collective bargaining for freelancers and action against bogus self-employment.
Calls on the Commission to monitor EU AI rules to balance AI providers' data access with journalist protection.
Encourages unions and media organisations to address AI in newsrooms through social dialogue.
Calls for funding for journalists' AI literacy and European Journalism Academies.
